title: Approval processes and Flow-based approval patterns
objectives: Explain a classic approval process: entry, steps, initial submission (record lock), and final approval actions.
Contrast Flow Approval Processes as the modern Flow-based alternative Salesforce Help tells you to try.
Choose Submit for Approval from a Flow versus a record-triggered or autolaunched Flow Approval Process.
State that both classic and Flow Approval Processes do not consume automation credits or orchestration runs, per Help.
diagnostic_question: Discount over 20% needs manager then finance, the record must lock while pending, and routing should depend on region. Do you start with a classic approval process or a Flow Approval Process, and why?
definition: A classic approval process automates how records are approved: steps, who must approve, and actions at submit, approval, rejection, and recall. By default the record locks on initial submission. Flow Approval Processes are a Flow-based alternative that can trigger on record changes, support dynamic routing, Apex extensibility, and detailed logging. Help says both do not consume automation credits or orchestration runs. ([Classic terminology](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_terminology.htm); [Prepare classic approvals](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_prep_org.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers still ask lock, submitter, and step actions. They also ask why Salesforce now pushes Flow Approval Processes for dynamic routing. ‘I would just email the manager’ is a weak answer.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a building-permit office. The applicant submits plans (submit). The file is locked in the clerk’s cage so nobody quietly redraws them (record lock). Inspectors stamp in order (steps). Final approval actions are the permit sticker. Classic approvals are a fixed counter with object-tied steps. A Flow Approval Process is a routed inspection that can change streets from data—still a permit, not a random after-save Flow that emails someone.
deeper_explanation: Help: a classic approval process specifies each step, from whom to request approval, and what to do at each point. Initial submission actions run when a user first submits; by default the record is locked. Final approval actions run when all required approvals are obtained. Record locking prevents users from editing regardless of FLS or sharing; only admins can edit locked records by default. ([Terminology](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_terminology.htm))

Help repeatedly: try Flow Approval Processes, a modern alternative with a Flow-based interface, record-change triggers, Apex extensibility, detailed logging, dynamic routing based on data and business rules, and visibility into bottlenecks. Classic processes are tied to specific objects with limited condition support. Like classic, Flow Approval Processes do not consume automation credits or orchestration runs. ([Prepare classic](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.approvals_prep_org.htm))

Flow Types: Record-Triggered After Save Flow Approval Process launches when a record is created or updated. Autolaunched Flow Approval Process launches from Apex, REST, custom buttons, or links and includes recordId, submitter, and submissionComments inputs. ([Flow Types](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.flow_concepts_type.htm))

A regular Flow can still call Submit for Approval (classic) or, in later releases, an Action that calls an autolaunched Flow Approval Process after gathering data. That is a pattern, not a replacement for understanding lock and steps. ([Call from a Flow](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_automate_flow_call_flow_approval_process_from_a_flow_dynamic_action.htm))

Classic approvals remain available in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions (Help). Do not announce a retirement date that Salesforce has not published; Help’s message is to try the Flow-based alternative.

mental_model.analogy: A building-permit office: submit plans, lock the file, inspectors in sequence, final sticker. Classic = fixed counter; Flow Approval Process = routed inspection that can change streets from the data.

Flow Approval Processes are not the same as a random email-in-Flow.

Unanimous group behavior and recall features are release-sensitive—Needs verification.

claims.claim: A classic approval process defines steps, approvers, and actions. Initial submission locks the record by default. Final approval actions run when required approvals are obtained.
Record locking prevents users from editing a pending record regardless of FLS or sharing; only admins can edit locked records by default.

Salesforce Help presents Flow Approval Processes as a modern alternative with Flow UI, record-change triggers, dynamic routing, Apex extensibility, and logging. Like classic, they do not consume automation credits or orchestration runs.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Classic approvals are object-tied steps with lock on submit and final actions. Flow Approval Processes are the Help-endorsed Flow-based alternative for dynamic routing and record-triggered start. Neither consumes automation credits per Help. A regular email Flow is not an approval process.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start from the business need: lock, audit, multi-step approvers. Classic: initial submission locks, steps request approvers, final actions run. If routing must change from data or we want a record-triggered Flow Approval Process, I follow Help’s ‘try Flow Approval Processes’ note. I can still Submit for Approval from a screen Flow when a classic process already exists. I do not announce retirement. I keep the process as metadata and the Opportunity as data.

terminology.plain: What happens when the record is first submitted, including the default lock.

terminology.non_example: Final approval field update to Closed Won.

terminology.plain: Users cannot edit the record while it is pending, even if FLS and sharing would allow it.

interview_questions.question: Walk a classic approval process from submit to final approval.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: If the record meets entry criteria, submit runs initial actions and locks by default. Steps request approvers. When all required approvals are done, final approval actions run. Rejection and recall have their own actions.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use Help terminology: process, steps, initial submission, lock, final actions, process instance. I mention page layout Submit for classic. I say lock ignores FLS and sharing for normal users. I do not skip reject testing. I keep the definition as metadata and the record as data.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ Opportunity discount: lock on submit, manager step, finance step, final field update.
follow_ups: Who can edit a locked record?

interview_questions.question: Why does Salesforce Help tell you to try Flow Approval Processes?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: They are Flow-based, can start on record changes, support dynamic routing and logging, and do not consume automation credits or orchestration runs. Classic is object-tied with limited conditions.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I quote the Important note rather than a blog. I do not declare classic dead. I map dynamic Region__c routing to that contrast. I mention Flow Types: record-triggered after-save versus autolaunched with recordId, submitter, comments. Feature details are release-sensitive so I say I would re-read current Help.

interview_questions.question: Sales can change Amount while a discount is pending. They are not admins. What do you check?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Whether the record is locked, whether unlock already ran, and whether they are actually an admin. Lock should block edits regardless of FLS and sharing.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open the record’s approval history. If there is no instance, they never submitted. If pending and unlocked, I inspect initial submission actions. I test as that user, not as myself. I do not start by changing OWD. If this is a Flow Approval Process, I verify current lock behavior in Help instead of assuming classic defaults.

follow_ups: What if a Flow updated Amount?

interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Submit for Approval action using the record Id, plus a fault path. I do not rebuild lock with Assignments.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: If the org instead wants Flow-based approvals, I use an Action to an autolaunched Flow Approval Process and pass recordId, submitter, and submissionComments. I still gate any record-triggered start with entry criteria. I test fail paths because Help lists Submit for Approval as an element that can fail.

interview_questions.question: When is an email-in-Flow the wrong approval design?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When you need lock, formal steps, and an instance history. Email does not lock the file or create a process instance.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use the permit-office analogy and say where it breaks. If the business only wants a heads-up, email or a Task may be enough—and I say so. If they say ‘approval’ and still want Amount frozen, I insist on an approval process. I mention credits only to correct a rumor: Help says these approval types do not consume orchestration runs.

interview_questions.question: Opportunities keep submitting for approval on every save. Diagnose.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A record-triggered Flow or Flow Approval Process is starting without tight entry criteria, or Submit for Approval sits on an unfiltered after-save Flow.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I open Explorer (AUTO-010) and look for Submit actions. I add updated-to-meet on the discount threshold. I check whether final approval field updates retrigger another submit. I do not deactivate all approvals as step one in production.
interview_questions.example: After-save Flow Submit for Approval with no Start conditions.

interview_questions.question: How do you explain metadata versus data for approvals?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The process or Flow Approval Process is metadata you deploy. The Opportunity and each process instance are data. Deploying a process does not submit records.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Change sets move the definition. History rows stay in the org. Tests use LAB_ Opportunities. I do not copy production pending instances into a sandbox as a substitute for UAT. Lock state is runtime data.
interview_questions.example: Retrieving the approval process XML does not include Tuesday’s pending discount.
follow_ups: What happens to in-flight instances if you deactivate?
Needs verification: say you would read current Help.

interview_questions.question: A Java developer asks for a state machine. Map it to Salesforce approvals.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Classic or Flow Approval Processes are the platform state machine: submitted, locked, steps, approved/rejected. I would not hand-roll statuses in a Flow unless the business is not actually an approval.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map states to instance status and steps to nodes. I map transitions to approve/reject/recall. I warn that Flow Approval Processes are the extensible path Help is investing in. I do not invent a retirement date. I mention fault paths if Submit is called from a Flow. I keep routing data-driven when using Flow approvals.
